data.body:
Merged as 2318.

Root cause confirmed in source rather than inferred: scripts aside, src/rebar/_commands/_init_ensures.py deliberately UNSETS gc.auto on the tracker and sets gc.autoDetach=false, so a triggered git gc --auto runs FOREGROUND during a rebar write and can pack a just-committed blob. The test then failed on its own precondition (assert loose_object.is_file()) before exercising the fail-closed behaviour it guards.

Both shapes are now CONSTRUCTED, not hoped for:
- loose: gc is frozen before the ticket under test is written, so looseness is by construction rather than by luck.
- packed: a pack is written containing ONLY that blob (git pack-objects fed the single oid), the loose copy is dropped, git cat-file -e confirms the object now resolves solely from the pack, then the pack is deleted. git gc is not used — it is threshold-dependent and cannot deterministically induce the shape.

The plan review caught that a whole repack would have taken the commit and trees too, so the view would raise for a missing TREE rather than for this blob — passing for the wrong reason, the same false-pass class as c100. The assertion now matches the ticket's own *-CREATE.json path instead of the generic phrase.

RED proofs by real mutation: view stops failing closed -> both shapes fail; pack step neutered -> ONLY the packed case fails, proving that shape is genuinely constructed and not a duplicate of loose; blob left intact -> both fail. Broad suite 15366 passed, 0 failed.
